---
title: "Research"
---

At LIAC, we develop artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods for chemical reasoning, synthesis planning, molecular and materials discovery, and experimental optimization. We aim to connect predictive models to the decisions that chemists make and, ultimately, to experiments that generate new knowledge.

Our main research directions include:

- language models, chemical reasoning, and tool-augmented agents;
- reaction prediction, synthesis planning, and reaction-space navigation;
- generative molecular design with synthesis constraints;
- adaptive experimentation for reactions, catalysis, and materials.

## Selected Research Highlights

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [Synthegy: strategy-aware chemical reasoning](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matt.2026.102812)

**Matter, 2026.** Large language models guide chemical search algorithms using strategies written in natural language, enabling steerable retrosynthesis and reaction-mechanism elucidation.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matt.2026.102812) · [Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08537)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-026-01200-4)

**Nature Machine Intelligence, 2026.** Saturn combines the Mamba architecture with augmented memory to learn more from each scored molecule and directly optimize high-fidelity objectives.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-026-01200-4) · [Code](https://github.com/schwallergroup/saturn)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [TANGO: direct optimization of constrained synthesizability](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-026-00959-1)

**Nature Computational Science, 2026.** TANGO guides generative models toward molecules that use required starting materials or intermediates, making synthesizability part of the design objective.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-026-00959-1)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [Swarm intelligence for chemical-reaction optimization](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chempr.2026.103035)

**Chem, 2026.** α-PSO combines interpretable particle-swarm dynamics with machine-learning guidance for parallel experimental optimization.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chempr.2026.103035) · [Code](https://github.com/schwallergroup/alphaswarm)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [Highly parallel optimization of chemical reactions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61803-0)

**Nature Communications, 2025.** Minerva couples Bayesian optimization with automated 96-well experimentation to navigate large reaction-condition spaces.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61803-0) · [Code](https://github.com/schwallergroup/minerva)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [A multi-modal transformer for predicting global minimum adsorption energy](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58499-7)

**Nature Communications, 2025.** AdsMT predicts global minimum adsorption energies without enumerating binding sites and uses cross-attention to identify favorable adsorption locations.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58499-7)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [Data-driven synthesis predictions of colloidal nanocrystal shapes](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.4c17283)

**Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2025.** Machine learning, electronic-lab-notebook data, Bayesian optimization, and experiments were combined to navigate copper-nanocrystal synthesis.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.4c17283)
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### [ChemCrow: augmenting large-language models with chemistry tools](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-024-00832-8)

**Nature Machine Intelligence, 2024.** ChemCrow demonstrated how a language model can plan and execute complex chemistry tasks by using purpose-built tools.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-024-00832-8) · [Code](https://github.com/ur-whitelab/chemcrow-public)
:::
:::
